text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- Turkey will never forgive Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller for carrying the Islamists to power in a coalition. Turkey is going through the most tense period in its history caused by the Islamist's coming to power.
- Leading business organisations have strongly criticised the Islamist-led government and distanced themselves from the ruling alliance.
HURRIYET
- A "terrorist" attacked a mass-circulation newspaper following Ciller's campaign to single out the media as a target.
- Senior commanders in the Turkish army held a meeting on the rise of radical voices in the Islamist Welfare Party.
MILLIYET
- Milliyet daily sues Ciller for compensation for her statements targeting the paper at a party rally held in Istanbul at the weekend.
YENI YUZYIL
- Turkish aircrafts bombed northern Iraq in a cross-border operation against rebel Kurds operating from the region.
- A deal to build a natural gas pipeline to transfer Turkmen natural gas to Europe via Iran and Turkey will be signed on Tuesday.
RADIKAL
- The textile sector is top of the list of tax dodgers, followed by the restaurant and tourism sector.
CUMHURIYET
- Welfare is gearing up to call a referandum on whether to implement a secularist compulsory education plan sponsored by the military-dominated National Security Council (MGK).
- The background of people buying ports under the government's privatisation scheme will be monitored to ensure they are not bought up by organised crime groups.
DUNYA
- The Central Bank foreign currency reserves have melted rapidly in 1997. The total national reserve dropped to $26 billion from $28.8 billion in four months.
- The ready-to wear sector is investing in the underdeveloped southeast after a huge dam project in the region helped increase cotton production.
ZAMAN
- State Minister Abdullah Gul says the countries of the D-8 -- a group of eight Moslem states -- will produce their own technology.
